arxiv-1509-00155.title: Engineering Bright Solitons to Enhance the Stability of Two-Component Bose-Einstein Condensates
arxiv-1509-00155.creator: R. Radha ∗,1, P. S. Vinayagam 1, J. B. Sudharsan 1, Wu-Ming Liu †,2, Boris A. Malomed ††,3
arxiv-1509-00155.description: Abstract We consider a system of coupled Gross-Pitaevskii (GP) equations describing a binary quasi-one-dimensional Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) with intrinsic time-dependent attractive interactions, placed in a time-dependent expulsive parabolic potential, in a special case when the system is integrable (a deformed Manakov’s system).

arxiv-2007-06595.title: Crystallographic Interacting Topological Phases and Equivariant Cohomology: To assume or not to assume
arxiv-2007-06595.creator: Daniel Sheinbaum, Omar Antolín Camarena
arxiv-2007-06595.description: Abstract For symmorphic crystalline interacting gapped systems we derive a classification under adiabatic evolution. This classification is complete for non-degenerate ground states. For the degenerate case we discuss some invariants given by equivariant characteristic classes. We do not assume an emergent relativistic field theory nor that phases form a topological spectrum.

arxiv-2109-02909.title: BioNetExplorer: Architecture-Space Exploration of Bio-Signal Processing Deep Neural Networks for Wearables
arxiv-2109-02909.creator: Bharath Srinivas Prabakaran 1, Asima Akhtar 1, Semeen Rehman, Osman Hasan, and Muhammad Shafique
arxiv-2109-02909.description: Abstract Deep Learning (DL) has been shown to be highly effective in solving various problems across numerous applications and domains, such as autonomous driving and image recognition. Due to the advent of DL, plenty of research works have explored the applicability of DL, more specifically Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), to solve pattern recognition and computer vision challenges.

arxiv-2109-07065.title: From Six Functors Formalisms to Derived Motivic Measures
arxiv-2109-07065.creator: Joshua F. Lieber
arxiv-2109-07065.description: Abstract . In this paper, we generally describe a method of taking an abstract six functors formalism in the sense of Khan or Cisinski-Déglise, and outputting a derived motivic measure in the sense of Campbell-Wolfson-Zakharevich. In particular, we use this framework to define a lifting of the Gillet-Soulé motivic measure.

arxiv-2110-11198.title: Temporal Motifs in Patent Opposition and Collaboration Networks
arxiv-2110-11198.creator: Penghang Liu, Naoki Masuda, Tomomi Kito, Ahmet Erdem Sarıyüce
arxiv-2110-11198.description: Abstract Patents are intellectual properties that reflect innovative activities of companies and organizations. The literature is rich with the studies that analyze the citations among the patents and the collaboration relations among companies that own the patents. However, the adversarial relations between the patent owners are not as well investigated.

arxiv-2206-02112.title: Kinetic model description of dissipation and recovery in collagen fibrils under cyclic loading
arxiv-2206-02112.creator: Amir Suhail, Anuradha Banerjee, R. Rajesh
arxiv-2206-02112.description: Abstract Collagen fibrils, when subjected to cyclic loading, are known to exhibit hysteretic behaviour with energy dissipation that is partially recovered on relaxation. In this paper, we develop a kinetic model for a collagen fibril incorporating presence of hidden loops and stochastic fragmentation as well as reformation of sacrificial bonds.

arxiv-2306-16875.title: Gravitational collapse and accretion flows in the hub filament system G323.46-0.08
arxiv-2306-16875.creator: Yingxiu Ma, Jianjun Zhou, Jarken Esimbek, Willem Baan, Dalei Li, Xindi Tang, Yuxin He, Weiguang Ji, Dongdong Zhou, Gang Wu, Kadirya Tursun, Toktarkhan Komesh
arxiv-2306-16875.description: Abstract We studied the hub-filament system G323.46-0.08 based on archival molecular line data from the SEDIGISM 13 CO survey and infrared data from the GLIMPSE, MIPS, and Hi-GAL surveys. G323.46-0.08 consists of three filaments, F-north, F-west, and F-south, that converge toward the central high-mass clump AGAL 323.459-0.079. F-west and Part 1 of the F-south show clear large-scale velocity gradients 0.

arxiv-2407-04702.title: On the Nonexistence of Centered Co-Circular Central Configurations With Three Unequal masses
arxiv-2407-04702.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by . This paper examines the existence of centered co-circular central configurations in the general power-law potential n n -body problem. We prove the nonexistence of such configurations when the system consists of n − 3 n-3 equal masses and three arbitrary masses, under the condition that the three special masses are distinct or, if two of them are equal, not arranged in a specific manner.

arxiv-2407-13720.title: Design of a Thomson scattering diagnostic for the SMART tokamak
arxiv-2407-13720.creator: M. Kaur, A. Diallo, B. LeBlanc, J. Segado-Fernandez, E. Viezzer, Roger Huxford, A. Mancini, D. J. Cruz-Zabala, M. Podesta, J. W. Berkery, M. Garcia-Muñoz
arxiv-2407-13720.description: Abstract We describe the design of a Thomson scattering (TS) diagnostic to be used on the SMall Aspect Ratio Tokamak (SMART). SMART is a spherical tokamak being commissioned in Spain that aims to explore positive triangularity (PT) and negative triangularity (NT) plasma scenarios at a low aspect ratio.

arxiv-2410-02681.title: Understanding and Mitigating Miscalibration in Prompt Tuning for Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2410-02681.creator: Shuoyuan Wang, Yixuan Li, Hongxin Wei
arxiv-2410-02681.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shuoyuan Wang, Yixuan Li, Hongxin Wei. Confidence calibration is critical for the safe deployment of machine learning models in the real world. However, such issue in vision-language models like CLIP, particularly after fine-tuning, has not been fully addressed.

arxiv-2504-02009.title: Urban Computing in the Era of Large Language Models
arxiv-2504-02009.creator: Zhonghang Li, Lianghao Xia, Xubin Ren, Jiabin Tang, Tianyi Chen, Yong Xu, Chao Huang
arxiv-2504-02009.description: Abstract . Urban computing has emerged as a multidisciplinary field that harnesses data-driven technologies to address challenges and improve urban living. Traditional approaches, while beneficial, often face challenges with generalization, scalability, and contextual understanding. The advent of Large Language Models (LLMs) offers transformative potential in this domain.

arxiv-2505-23386.title: VModA : An Effective Framework for Adaptive NSFW Image Moderation
arxiv-2505-23386.creator: Han Bao, Qinying Wang, Zhi Chen, Qingming Li, Xuhong Zhang, Changjiang Li, Zonghui Wang, Shouling Ji, Wenzhi Chen
arxiv-2505-23386.description: Abstract Not Safe/Suitable for Work (NSFW) content is rampant on social networks and poses serious harm to citizens, especially minors. Current detection methods mainly rely on deep learning-based image recognition and classification. However, NSFW images are now presented in increasingly sophisticated ways, often using image details and complex semantics to obscure their true nature or attract more views.

arxiv-2508-00739.title: Shaping circuit for improving linearity, bandwidth, and dynamic range in ToT-based detectors Journal: Nuclear Physics B
arxiv-2508-00739.creator: J. Peña-Rodríguez, J. Förtsch, C. Pauly, K.-H. Kampert
arxiv-2508-00739.description: Abstract The quantitative measurement of energy deposits in particle detectors, particularly in calorimeters, is usually accomplished with the help of Analog-to-Digital converters (ADCs) due to their precision, wide measurement range, and good linearity. However, drawbacks such as power consumption, data volume, and bandwidth limit their use in the next generation of high-energy physics experiments.

arxiv-2509-02897.title: Atmospheric CO 2 \text{CO}_{\text{2}} Ice in the Martian Polar Regions: Physical and Spectral Properties From Mars Climate Sounder Observations
arxiv-2509-02897.description: Abstract CO 2 \text{CO}_{\text{2}} ice clouds are important for polar energy balance and the carbon dioxide cycle on Mars. However, uncertainties remain regarding their physical and radiative properties, which control how polar CO 2 \text{CO}_{\text{2}} clouds interact with the global Martian climate. Here, we use Mars Climate Sounder (MCS) observations of atmospheric radiance to estimate these physical and radiative properties.

britannica-1911-wuchang.title: Wuchang (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-wuchang.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-wuchang.description: Article 'Wuchang' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 28), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. It is one of the three cities, Wuchang, Hanyang and Hankow, which stand together at the mouth of the Han river, and is situated on the right bank of the river Yangtsze, almost directly opposite the foreign settlement of Hankow. It is the seat of the provincial government of the two Hu or Hu-kwang, as these provinces are collectively termed, at the head of which is a viceroy.

europmc-pmc2131663.title: NUMBER OF GLOMERULI IN KIDNEY OF ADULT WHITE RAT UNILATERALLY NEPHRECTOMIZED IN EARLY LIFE.
europmc-pmc2131663.creator: Moore RA.
europmc-pmc2131663.description: Unilateral nephrectomy during the period of active nephrogenesis in the white rat has no effect on the total number of glomeruli which will be formed in the opposite kidney.

pmc-10669283.title: Enrichment of Deleterious Mutated Genes Involved in Ciliary Function and Histone Modification in Brain Cancer Patient-Derived Xenograft Models
pmc-10669283.creator: Hyeongsun Jeong, Hyo Eun Moon, Seongmin Yun, Seung Woo Cho, Hye Ran Park, Sung-Hye Park, Kyungjae Myung, Taejoon Kwon, Sun Ha Paek
pmc-10669283.description: Patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models, which can retain the characteristics of original tumors in an in vivo-mimicking environment, have been developed to identify better treatment options. However, although original tumors and xenograft tissues mostly share oncogenic mutations and global gene expression patterns, their detailed mutation profiles occasionally do not overlap, indicating that selection occurs in the xenograft environment.

pmc-10698562.title: Pharmacokinetics and therapeutic target attainment of vancomycin in pediatric post-liver transplant patients
pmc-10698562.creator: Ronaldo Morales Junior, Vanessa D'Amaro Juodinis, Daniela Carla de Souza, Silvia Regina Cavani Jorge Santos
pmc-10698562.description: IntroductionVancomycin is widely prescribed to treat or prevent Gram-positive infections in pediatric liver transplant recipients. The objective of this prospective cohort study is to describe vancomycin pharmacokinetics and to evaluate the therapeutic target attainment after initial dose regimen.Materials and methodsPatients with previous renal injury were excluded. Vancomycin therapy started with 40‒60 mg/kg/day.

pmc-11393569.title: A case of acute lithium poisoning and hypermagnesemia involving advanced colon cancer-induced colonic obstruction
pmc-11393569.creator: Hideo Takayama, Takuya Komura, Taro Kawane, Toshiki Matsuo, Makiko Kimura, Masashi Nishikawa, Kiyoki Kitagawa, Wataru Omi, Kenichi Sakajiri, Ichiro Onishi, Satoru Sakagami, Taro Yamashita, Takashi Kagaya
pmc-11393569.description: An 83-year-old woman presented with disturbance of consciousness and hand tremor. She had taken lithium carbonate 300 mg/day for bipolar disorder and magnesium oxide 660 mg/day for constipation. Blood tests revealed lithium poisoning, hypermagnesemia and acute kidney injury. Computed tomography showed colonic obstruction caused by cancer of the descending colon.

pmc-11461033.title: Idiopathic Spinal Epidural Hematoma: A Near Miss of a Rare Entity
pmc-11461033.creator: Chin Y Wells, Benjamin Heigle, Prabhneet Pannu, Stephen Pham, Ziad Ghneim, Neelakanta Dadi
pmc-11461033.description: Spinal epidural hematomas (SEH) are rare, and cases with a spontaneous etiology are even more infrequent. Management of spontaneous SEH varies, with surgical or conservative approaches determined by the severity of deficits and symptom resolution. Adverse prognostic factors may include thoracic segment location, anticoagulation use, severe neurologic deficits at admission, sphincter dysfunction, and rapid progression.

pmc-12634690.title: Control mechanism of the surrounding rock structure of multisection stopes in steeply dipping coal seams under overburden transient changes excitation
pmc-12634690.creator: Yongping Wu, Jingyu Huangfu, Shenghu Luo, Yepeng Tang, Zhuangzhuang Yan, Chengyang Tian, Tong Wang
pmc-12634690.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The mining cycle of multi-section stopes in steeply dipping coal seams is protracted, and the ground pressure appearance is complex.This study utilized physical simulation and theoretical analysis to investigate the surrounding rock structural evolution mechanism in multi-section longwall stopes of steeply dipping coal seams, the mechanical response of barrier pillars under the transient change excitation of the overburden spatial structure, and determine the key dimensions of barrier pillars for controlling the surrounding rock structure.

pmc-12649694.title: Diagnostic Support in Dentistry Through Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Review
pmc-12649694.creator: Alessio Danilo Inchingolo, Grazia Marinelli, Arianna Fiore, Liviana Balestriere, Claudio Carone, Francesco Inchingolo, Massimo Corsalini, Daniela Di Venere, Andrea Palermo, Angelo Michele Inchingolo, Gianna Dipalma, Chengfei Zhang, Kwang Woo Ahn
pmc-12649694.description: Background/Objectives: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into dental diagnostics is rapidly evolving, offering opportunities to improve diagnostic precision, reproducibility, and accessibility of care. This systematic review examined the clinical performance of AI-based diagnostic tools in dentistry compared with traditional methods, with particular attention to radiographic assessment, orthodontic classification, periodontal disease detection, and other relevant specialties.

pmc-13085569.title: Oral–maxillofacial and cervical schwannomas: a retrospective cohort analysis with a rare intraosseous case
pmc-13085569.creator: Xiaomin Hu, Dongxiang Wang, Zhenglong Tang
pmc-13085569.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the clinical, pathological, and immunohistochemical characteristics of schwannomas (SCHs) in the oral, maxillofacial, and cervical regions to provide a reference for their diagnosis and clinical management.Materials and methodsWe retrospectively analyzed 20 patients with oral, maxillofacial, and cervical SCHs treated at our institution between January 2019 and December 2025. Clinical history, presenting symptoms, and relevant auxiliary examinations were collected.

pmc-13145092.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1888 EXPLORING THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN CHRONIC DISEASES AND STROKE INCIDENCE: APOPULATION-BASED STUDY IN ANDALUSIA
pmc-13145092.creator: Alfredo Palomino Garcia, Diego Villagran Sancho, Jose Ramón Torres-Martín, Jose Manuel Velarde_gestera, German Escobar Rodriguez, Inmaculada Mora-Jiménez, Jose Luis García-Garmendia, Auxiliadora Caballero-García
pmc-13145092.description: Background and aimsStroke is one of the leading causes of death and disability worldwide, posing a major economic and social burden on patients and society. In Andalusia, Spain, it remains the primary cause of mortality. Its occurrence is strongly influenced by both non-modifiable and modifiable risk factors, many of which coexist with chronic diseases.

pmc-13178368.title: Evaluating convolutional neural network models for automated abdominal aortic calcification scoring in chronic kidney disease patients across multiple centers
pmc-13178368.creator: Zhenhong Shao, Mingrui Song, Beibei He, Hupo Yi, Aijing Li, Ge Chen, Zhehao Zhang, Yuning Pan
pmc-13178368.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAbdominal aortic calcification (AAC) is a condition particularly common in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). This study aims to assess the accuracy and generalizability of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in automating AAC scoring in CKD patients.MethodsAbdominal aortic X-ray images from five hospitals were employed to evaluate three CNN architectures (DenseNet, RegNet and ResNet) using the internal hold-out and five-fold cross-validation method.

pmc-13292152.title: Neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)-related index as an indicator of periprosthetic joint infection
pmc-13292152.creator: Tingrun Cui, Yongjian Liang, Zeyu Feng, Libo Hao, Guoqiang Zhang, Ming Ni, Jing Sheng, Dihua Shangguan, Jiying Chen, Jun Fu

pmc-13295034.title: Lacrimal Drainage Catheter Coated with Mitomycin C to Inhibit Fibrosis after Canalicular Laceration Repair
pmc-13295034.creator: Huanhuan Xu, Liang Lu, Xueying Kong, Rui Wu, Hu Meng, Dekui Ren, Jun Gu, Yong Wu, Yirui Ge
pmc-13295034.description: Canalicular lacerations represent a common ocular emergency that can lead to significant complications if not managed promptly and effectively. Silicone stents are the most commonly chosen option due to their favorable characteristics. However, postoperative complications, such as canalicular stenosis, remain prevalent, necessitating the exploration of additional therapeutic strategies.

pmc-13445811.title: A systematic review focusing on how medical researchers report variables in risk scores or models to predict prognosis of patients after percutaneous coronary intervention
pmc-13445811.creator: Hong-Liang Zhao, Jing Shi, Guo-Qing Qi, Ming-Qi Zheng, Gang Wang
pmc-13445811.description: BackgroundVariability in risk variable selection for prognostic scores/models after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is poorly characterized. This systematic review examined how researchers report such variables and compared selection between Caucasian and non-Caucasian populations.MethodsWe searched PubMed/MEDLINE (inception to December 2025) for English-language studies developing, validating, or comparing risk scores/models for post-PCI prognosis. Data were synthesized descriptively.

pmc-13595978.title: A novel highly specific qPCR assay for distinguishing HBV cccDNA from rcDNA following bisulfite pretreatment
pmc-13595978.creator: Ning Sun, Zhili Wang, Zach Heimer, Chris Wenner, Selena Y. Lin, Heidi Y. Ding, Roman Kubas, You-Yu Liu, Eliza Qiu, Hsin-Ni Liu, Hsu-Chin Hung, Wenya Huang, Tianlun Zhou, Daryl T.-Y. Lau, Ying-Hsiu Su, Haitao Guo
pmc-13595978.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The persistence of covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) underlies chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and remains as the major barrier to achieving a functional cure. An accurate and sensitive quantification of cccDNA is critical for evaluating therapeutic strategies. The conventional quantitative PCR (qPCR) lacks specificity to distinguish cccDNA from viral relaxed circular DNA (rcDNA) and other replicative intermediates, while nuclease pretreatment (e.g., plasmid-safe ATP-dependent nuclease, exonucleases I/III, or T5 exonuclease) may either incompletely digest rcDNA and/or risk over-digesting cccDNA.

pmc-13625248.title: Augmenting medical data interpretation with Large Language Models (LLMs): a comparative analysis of patient empowerment, information processing, and technology acceptance
pmc-13625248.creator: Pouyan Esmaeilzadeh
pmc-13625248.description: BackgroundMedical data interpretation traditionally relies on healthcare professionals as intermediaries, which can limit patient autonomy and engagement. Large Language Models (LLMs) present an opportunity to transform this paradigm by enabling direct patient access to AI-generated interpretations; however, comparative research on their effectiveness across different medical data types and communication modalities remains limited.
